subject: AFS
course_description: An introductory course on African Studies. May be repeated for credit when topic varies.
course_notes: (Same as WGS 285W 3, AAS 285W 1) African Feminist Theories This course considers issues, debates, and methodologies in African feminist theorizing as students encounter the diversity of feminisms in Africa. Students will analyze frameworks such as Motherism, African womanism, Stiwanism, Femininitude, and Nego-feminism, and investigate relationships between coloniality and gender, women and revolution, storytelling and theory. Engaging interdisciplinary texts including critical writing, interviews, poetry, oral tales, memoir and film, this course considers the ways in which thinker-practitioners have challenged Eurocentric feminisms and enacted what Obioma Nnaemeka calls "the simultaneous gesture of theorizing practice and practicing theory" (2003, 377). Throughout the semester, students will encounter themes of motherhood, sexuality, religion, class, solidarities, technology, love, power and imagined futures.
